page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at 2.6 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying on external storage solutions, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate average multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the middle 50% tier. However, single-core performance is a relative bottleneck, with stress-ng single-core results ranking in the bottom 10%. Memory performance is mixed; while small-block cached read bandwidth is average, large-block uncached read and write bandwidth tests show weaker performance, placing in the bottom 25%. Computational tasks like software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing perform at average levels, whereas text processing shows weaker relative throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated AMD EPYC hardware profile offers a balanced mid-tier compute density without the premium cost of high-memory or GPU-accelerated instances. Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and average multi-threaded performance, this instance is suited for compute-bound workloads that do not require high single-core speeds or massive memory footprints. Suitable workloads include multi-threaded web serving, software compilation, medium-scale database operations, and general-purpose batch processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor with 32 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, this x86_64 instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps and lacks local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks place its multi-core capabilities, software compilation, and database operations in the average tier, though single-core performance and uncached large-block memory bandwidth are relatively weak. The instance offers a cost-effective option for multi-threaded, compute-heavy tasks that do not demand high single-core throughput or massive memory allocations. It is best suited for workloads such as multi-threaded web serving, batch processing, and software compilation.
